name: Andorra
summary: A tiny state in the Pyrenees ruled since 1278 by two co-princes: the bishop of Urgell and (now) the president of France.

knownFor.label: Co-princes
knownFor.note: Shared rule set by an agreement of 1278.

location.value: In the Pyrenees between Spain and France, landlocked.

terrain.value: High Pyrenees valleys; the whole country is above 840 m.

resources.value: Tourism (ski resorts), duty-free shopping, banking; once tobacco farming.

disasters.value: Floods and avalanches; a severe flood in 1982.

population.value: About 90,000 (July 2026 estimate); about two-thirds of residents are not Andorran.

urbanisation.value: Andorra la Vella and Escaldes-Engordany form one urban area.

migration.value: Most residents came from Spain, Portugal and France.

economicBase.value: Tourism (about 8 million visitors a year), retail and banking.

tradeRoutes.value: Customs union with the EU for industrial products, since 1991.

wealth.value: A high-income economy, based on tourism, shopping and banking.

moneyAndTax.value: Uses the euro under a 2011 agreement with the EU (in force 2012); income tax legislation was announced in 2013.

inequality.value: Low inequality, but very high housing costs.

keyRulers.value: The two co-princes (French president and Bishop of Urgell).

institutions.value: The General Council (founded 1419); a constitution in force since 4 May 1993.

stability.value: Very stable; the country has been at peace for centuries.

eliteConflict.value: Little political conflict, with small parties and a tradition of consensus.

armyAndTech.value: No armed forces; France and Spain must respect its sovereignty and be consulted on threats.

majorWars.value: Neutral in the Second World War.

territoryChange.value: The borders have stayed the same since the Middle Ages.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to Spain and France; joined the UN in 1993.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded for this tiny state.

openness.value: Very open to tourism; its banking sector has tax haven status.

communicationTransport.value: No fixed-wing airport or railway station within the borders; heliports exist.

religion.value: Mostly Catholic; the Bishop of Urgell is a co-prince.

languageWriting.value: Catalan is the only official language, and Spanish, French and Portuguese are widely spoken.

artsArchitecture.value: Small Romanesque churches with bell towers (Santa Coloma, Sant Joan de Caselles).

socialStructure.value: A prosperous society where citizens are a minority.

sharedIdentity.value: Catalan-speaking mountain identity and pride in neutrality.

dailyLife.value: Stone houses; mountain dishes such as trinxat (cabbage and potato).

neighbours.value: Spain and France, in the Pyrenees mountains.

ideasReligions.value: Catalan culture and Catholic tradition shape the country’s identity.

colonisation.value: Shared sovereignty since the 1278 paréage agreement.

riseSignals.value: The paréage agreement of 1278 created the co-principality.

peakPeriod.value: Modern prosperity from tourism and shopping (1960s–).

declineSignals.value: None; it has kept its special status for over 700 years.

outcome.value: Still in existence; fully sovereign since the 1993 constitution.
